title: SEC Co. Supplies HBM Inspection Equipment to Micron; Samsung, SK Inline Orders Imminent
source_used: BigGo Finance (aggregated report citing Researchalum and NH Investment & Securities)
key_facts: South Korea's SEC Co., an X-ray inspection equipment maker, supplies HBM inspection equipment to Micron.
It sold eight manual HBM inspection systems to Micron in 2025.
It is validating inline (production-line) equipment with Samsung and SK Hynix; orders could come as early as Q1 2027 if it passes quality tests.
Taller HBM stacks (12-high in production, 16-high in qualification) need X-ray checks of internal bonds.
SEC posted a first-half operating loss of 7.7 billion won; Researchalum projects 2027 revenue of 85 billion won and a return to profit.
quote_evidence: South Korea's SEC Co., an industrial X-ray inspection equipment maker, has established a foothold in the global market by supplying HBM (High Bandwidth Memory) inspection equipment to U.S. memory semiconductor company Micron.
If the company is selected as a supplier and passes additional quality testing, orders could materialize as early as Q1 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: Memory makers need new ways to inspect taller HBM stacks; one small supplier is early in that market.
notes: Aggregator report; original Korean source and analysts not opened. Mix of company data and analyst projections.
